_comment: Coordinate reference system and grid definition for the site coordinates in
data/raw/sites/pts.shp. This file documents a PROPERTY OF THE RAW INPUT DATA: the
CRS in which the site coordinates were given to us.
It deliberately does NOT specify a map projection for plotting. The display
projection is our choice, is not yet decided (see repo issue #4), and will be
documented separately once it is. See `provenance.display_projection_note` below
for what the upstream product used, recorded as context only.

source_crs.name: WGS 84

ellipsoid.name: WGS 84
ellipsoid._note: WGS84's inverse flattening (298.257223563) differs slightly from GRS80's (298.257222101). The difference is ~0.1 mm in the semi-minor axis and is irrelevant at this grid's ~1 km spacing, but the two numbers are not typos for each other.

source_crs._axis_order_note: EPSG:4326 formally declares (latitude, longitude) axis order, but this file stores longitude first, matching the GDAL/PROJ traditional order. Pass `always_xy=True` (pyproj) or the equivalent when transforming, or coordinates will silently swap.
source_crs._wkt_status: UNVALIDATED. Neither pyproj nor any R spatial package (sf/terra/sp) is installable on the development workstation (issue #4), so this WKT string has not been round-tripped through a PROJ implementation. The authority code EPSG:4326 is the authoritative identifier; prefer resolving that over parsing this string. Validate on SCC before relying on the WKT.

grid.description: Sites lie on cell centres of the ~1 km geographic grid of the source product.

cell_centre_formula._note: lon_idx and lat_idx are the columns of that name in the processed site table, and are the exact representation of a site's position; the stored floats depart from true cell centres by up to 1.0e-6 degrees. Stated as a set of centre coordinates rather than an array indexing convention: the row orientation of the source GeoTIFFs has not been inspected, so no north-up/south-up claim is made here.

approximate_metric_spacing_m._note: 30 arcsec is near-constant in latitude but shrinks with cos(lat) in longitude. The grid is NOT equal-area across this domain.

grid_alignment.claim: All 8000 site coordinates lie on cell centres of the 1/120-degree lattice.
grid_alignment.method: Computed (lat, lon) index residuals from the nearest cell centre for all 8000 records of data/raw/sites/pts.shp, parsed directly from the .shp binary.
grid_alignment.result: 8000 of 8000 rows match, with maximum deviation 1.02e-06 degrees (about 0.11 m).

residual_explanation.claim: The ~1e-6 degree residual is consistent with float32 storage somewhere upstream.
residual_explanation.example: Site 1 stored latitude is 82.5458343506; the exact cell centre 85 - k/120 evaluates to 82.5458333333.

extent_consistency.claim: The stated extent, resolution and dimensions are mutually consistent.

sources: ORNL DAAC dataset guide, which states: "Geographic coordinates using WGS 84 datum (EPSG 4326)".
data/pts.prj, which declares GEOGCS["GCS_WGS_1984", DATUM["D_WGS_1984", SPHEROID["WGS_1984", 6378137.0, 298.257223563]]] and no projected coordinate system.

shapefile_agreement.claim: The site shapefile and the site table extracted from site_info.Rdata held identical coordinates.
shapefile_agreement.result: Compared element-wise before site_info.Rdata was retired: maximum difference 4.1e-13 degrees in longitude and 5.7e-14 in latitude, attributable to decimal truncation in the CSV extract. The shapefile is now the sole source; this record is kept only to document that no coordinate change accompanied the switch.

provenance.source_product: North American Land Carbon Reanalysis, 2012-2024 (Zhang et al. 2026), ORNL DAAC
provenance.received_via: Dongchen Zhang, who described the coordinates as "a MODIS-like coordinate system (0.008333 degree resolution for both latitude and longitude)".

display_projection_note._purpose: CONTEXT ONLY. This is not a property of our raw coordinates and is not a decision this file makes.
display_projection_note.text: For the figures in the published product, Dongchen used USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic (ESRI:102003, on NAD83) "to preserve the area across latitudes". Our own display projection is undecided; see repo issue #4. Note that ESRI:102003's nominal area of use is CONUS only, while 4360 of the 8000 sites fall outside a CONUS box. Albers Equal Area is area-true everywhere by construction, so an area-based argument survives that; what degrades away from the standard parallels (29.5, 45.5) is shape and orientation, e.g. a rotation of about +43 degrees for the northeast Greenland sites and -50 degrees for the western Aleutians.
